newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee retraces from peaks, still up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee retraces from peaks, still up.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures retraced from earlier sharp gains as speculators and funds took profits but still finished higher on Thursday on persistent buying.
By the finish, benchmark January, the most-active contract, stood $46 higher at $1,456 a tonne after rising early to the day's peak of $1,476 -- the highest level since mid-October.
"We had a bit of a setback because of fund selling and profit-taking but then I think it had a good buying around and we feel fairly positive about the market," said one trader.

January gapped $14 higher at the open and made its way up to $1,476, driven by broad-based buying led by the funds on the back of strong New York finish on Wednesday. "The funds bought this morning and then the market drifted away without support in New York," another said.
Volume was an impressive 10,110 lots, with January accounting for about 7,300 lots.
The January strength helped narrow the Nov/Jan spread to a low of $70 at one stage from Wednesday's $100 finish.
There were no fresh fundamental inputs behind today's rally but traders said persistent tight nearby supplies especially in the United States gave some background support.
U.S. certified coffee stocks have never been so low and fresh Central and South American coffee are not expected to hit the market until next month at the earliest.

Today's positive finish triggered a friendly chart signal but traders had hoped for the market to close above $1,470 to decisively alter the recent bearish run. January faced key chart resistance at $1,485-90 and then $1,500. Support is now seen in the $1,415 territory.
In physical news, the Association of Coffee Producing Countries' technical committee will review the market at this weekend's meeting in Costa Rica but no major market-moving news is expected.
